newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt makes proposal in metalworker dispute.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt makes proposal in metalworker dispute.

text.p: The Italian government, pushing to end a protracted pay dispute in the engineering and metalworking sector, made a proposal for a new contract on Monday after holding all-night talks with trade unions and employers.

"After several different meetings which took place overnight, the government, taking note of the significant progress that was made, presented a proposal to end the negotiations," Prime Minister Romano Prodi's office said in a statement.
The talks were suspended while unions and the employers' group Federmeccanica studied the new proposal.
The dispute, which began last June when the contract covering engineering and metal workers expired, involves some 1.7 million workers in a sector which accounts for 40 percent of industrial output.
Talks between sectoral unions FIM, FIOM and UILM and Federmeccanica resumed last Monday for the first time in more than a month to try to end the dispute.
Any deal is likely to set the tone for other pay accords and prove key to Italy's hopes of containing inflation.
Union leaders had hoped for a resolution by Sunday, but at the weekend said employers had raised fresh obstacles and called on the government to decide how to carry negotiations forward.
Prodi convened the talks at midnight on Monday (2300 GMT Sunday) and they ended at 8 a.m. (0700 GMT).
His office said the government had proposed a 30-month national contract period to replace a two-year contract which expired last June.
Under the proposal, the employers would make a one-off payment of 512,000 lire ($316) paid in two tranches during the first six months.
It would be followed by graduated monthly wage increases totalling 200,000 lire ($124) during the rest of the contract, the statement said.

Union leaders said they expected to give their response to the proposal later on Monday or Tuesday, and that a new meeting between the unions and Federmeccanica was likely to take place on Tuesday at the Labour Ministry.
"The government has forwarded a comprehensive proposal which we are evaluating," said Sergio Cofferatti, leader of CGIL trades union confederation.
